questions.q: What single, concrete thing did Driftwood Media's leadership ask for?
options: A single source of truth for subscriber growth, churn, and revenue, refreshed daily, without manual spreadsheet work
A complete replacement of their billing platform
A real-time, sub-second analytics system
A machine learning model to predict individual subscriber behavior
questions.explain: The request is deliberately unglamorous and realistic: one trustworthy, automated daily number, not a real-time or ML system.

questions.q: What two source systems does Driftwood's raw data currently come from?
options: Paper records and a fax machine
A billing platform (subscription events) and the product app's event logs (usage)
Two separate Snowflake accounts
A single unified data warehouse that just needs better reporting
questions.explain: Billing events and product usage events are the two real source systems this capstone's pipeline has to ingest and reconcile.

questions.q: Which tool in the stack is responsible for orchestrating the daily run, rather than relying on a person clicking "run"?
options: Git
Airflow
Terraform
Power BI
questions.explain: Airflow is the orchestration layer -- it's what makes the pipeline run automatically on a schedule instead of depending on manual execution.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the realistic starting condition this scenario is meant to mirror?
options: A single, already-unified data source needing no integration
Data already landing in two different source systems with two different shapes -- not a greenfield stack chosen from scratch
A company that has already fully solved its analytics problem
A company with no existing data systems at all
questions.explain: Unlike a greenfield project, Driftwood already has data in two different shapes from two different systems -- the realistic starting condition for most real analytics engineering jobs.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say this capstone deliberately introduces no brand-new tool beyond what you've already learned in this path?
options: Because the capstone is easier than the rest of the path
Because learning new tools is against the course's policy
Because Driftwood Media doesn't use any of those tools
Every lesson applies something already learned (Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Git/CI-CD, Terraform) to one continuous project, rather than teaching new tools from scratch
questions.explain: The capstone's point is integration and depth with known tools, not introducing new ones -- it's where everything already taught comes together.
